{"document_title":"Medicare Program; Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility Prospective Payment System for Federal Fiscal Year 2025 and Updates to the IRF Quality Reporting Program; Proposed Rule","agency":"Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), Department of Health and Human Services (HHS)","publication_date":"March 29, 2024","summary":"CMS proposes updates to the Inpatient Rehabilitation Facility (IRF) Prospective Payment System (PPS) for FY 2025 and changes to the IRF Quality Reporting Program (QRP). Key payment proposals include updated case-mix group (CMG) relative weights and average lengths of stay using FY 2023 claims and FY 2022 cost-report data (budget-neutral), a market basket-based update for FY 2025 (projected 3.2%) reduced by a productivity adjustment (0.4%) yielding a proposed 2.8% update, proposed labor-related share (74.2%), adoption of revised OMB CBSA delineations from OMB Bulletin No. 23-01 for the IRF wage index, a permanent 5% cap on wage-index decreases, use of FY 2021 hospital wage data for the FY 2025 pre-reclassification/pre-floor wage index, and a budget-neutral 3-year phase-out of the 14.9% rural adjustment for IRFs that shift from rural to urban under the new delineations. CMS proposes a FY 2025 standard payment conversion factor of $18,872 after budget-neutrality adjustments, updates to outlier policies including raising the outlier threshold from $10,423 (FY 2024) to $12,158 (FY 2025) to target ~3% outlier payments, and proposed national cost-to-charge ratio (CCR) urban/rural averages (0.406 urban, 0.492 rural) with a CCR ceiling of 1.52. For the IRF QRP beginning FY 2028, CMS proposes to add four standardized patient assessment items in the social determinants of health (SDOH) category (living situation, two food items, one utilities item), modify one transportation item, remove the Admission Class item, and requests information on future QRP measure concepts and an IRF star rating system. The rule includes methodologies, data sources, examples, and invites public comment by May 28, 2024."}
